loss_reason: Closed-lost to Replicate. Procurement chose Replicate for lower per-request pricing and existing engineering integration. Engineering cited Replicate's cheaper spot/GPU economics in benchmarked batch runs; security review called out missing SSO binding and token rotation automation as a risk but not decisive.
notes:
Stage: procurement -> closed-lost to Replicate. 
- POC summary: ran 2-week POC (Aug 19 - Sep 2). Benchmarks: Redwood latency 18-25ms p50 on t2 sequences; Replicate reported similar latency but ~30% lower token cost in our test harness.
- Customer quote (Head of ML): "Replicate gave us an easier on-ramp and cost profile that matched our budget assumptions."
- Sec ops: initial SOC2 docs fine; final security gating point was SSO/SAML mapping and automated key rotation (we proposed KMS integration), procurement prioritized existing vendor relationship.
- Internal churn: PM who sponsored Redwood left in July; new PM not evangelizing Redwood features (rollouts, fallback policies). No clear champion.
- Pricing: they asked for committed reserved capacity discount similar to Dedicated SKU; we quoted $180k ARR commit; procurement pushed back, asked for month-to-month.
- Competitive: Together evaluated for on-prem option but ultimately Replicate preferred for hybrid integration. Fireworks briefly in consideration for model registry only.
- Next actions we attempted: one final exec meeting 2024-09-28 (did not change decision), offered 60-day pilot discount, proposed SSO remediation plan and KMS onboarding timeline. Procurement signed Replicate PO on 2024-10-03.
- Sales notes: keep warm. Suggested re-engage at 6-month mark or on renewal discussions; send case study comparing long-term TCO and reliability fallbacks.
- Contact list: Head of ML (Asha Kapoor), Sr Eng Lead (Marcus Lin), Procurement (Diego Suarez).
